articles.title: Focused performance assessment predicts ability to perform open thoracic trauma procedures.
articles.authors: Andreatta P, Scott BL, Bradley M, Bowyer M
articles.study_type: Observational study with linear regression analysis
articles.sample_size: 1531 surgeons performing 11 thoracic procedures over 5 years
articles.outcomes: Identification of procedural elements that predict overall thoracic trauma operative performance; 46 of 96 procedural elements examined predicted 76% of overall performance variance
articles.take_home: A focused assessment of just 46 key procedural elements can predict three-quarters of a surgeon's overall ability to perform thoracic trauma operations, meaning training courses can reduce assessment burden whilst still identifying performance gaps. This suggests that structured procedural assessment is more reliable than surgeons' own perception of competence for determining readiness.

articles.title: Effect of a stabilized liquid ozone-containing formulation delivered through a hyaluronic acid/poly-D,L-lactide scaffold on early osteochondral repair in a rat model.
articles.authors: Kizkapan TB, Oguzkaya S, Misir A, Eken G, Sayer G, Bayrakcioglu OF, et al.
articles.population: Female Sprague-Dawley rats with osteochondral defects in the knee
articles.outcomes: Modified Mankin histological scores and residual cartilage damage area measured at 45 days post-surgery
articles.take_home: A scaffold containing ozone formulation showed better repair of cartilage damage compared to untreated defects and scaffolds alone in rats, though the study cannot confirm whether ozone itself caused the improvement.

articles.title: Microstructural Vulnerability of the Tibial Tubercle Apophysis During Growth Hormone Therapy: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Study Using Diffusion Tensor Imaging-MRI.
articles.authors: Fabricant PD, Beber SA, Perdomo-Luna C, Groff KD, Lu S, Kvist O, et al.
articles.population: Skeletally immature patients aged 6 years or older starting growth hormone therapy
articles.outcomes: Microstructural changes in the tibial tubercle measured by diffusion tensor imaging-MRI, including apparent diffusion coefficient and fractional anisotropy
articles.take_home: When children start growth hormone therapy, the bone growth plate at the shin develops temporary changes that peak around 8 months, which may explain why some children on this therapy get fractures there. Doctors should consider limiting impact sports during this vulnerable period.

articles.title: Mechanism-specific structural patterns in hospitalized severe mechanical open-globe injury: Implications for triage and operative preparedness in a 13-year tertiary referral cohort.
articles.authors: Qin C, Hua X, Zhu J, Yang T
articles.population: Patients hospitalised with severe mechanical open-globe injury
articles.outcomes: Final structural classification by Birmingham Eye Trauma Terminology; early visual status; visual improvement; length of stay; treatment completion
articles.take_home: The type of injury mechanism (such as industrial metal injury, falls, or fireworks) is strongly linked to the specific type of eye damage that occurs, with falls and fireworks causing globe ruptures that tend to have poorer visual outcomes and higher rates of incomplete treatment. Knowing the injury mechanism when a patient first arrives at hospital can help doctors prepare for what structural damage to expect and discuss realistic visual outcomes with patients.

articles.title: Fixation-specific modeling of age-frailty interactions to predict early mortality after hip fracture surgery.
articles.authors: Joachim K, Lin A, Gettleman B, Fice M, Hamad C, Abernethy C, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing surgery for hip fractures (femoral neck, pertrochanteric, or subtrochanteric fractures)
articles.outcomes: 30-day mortality rates across different surgical fixation methods and age-frailty combinations; secondary outcomes included transfusion rates, cardiopulmonary complications, and length of stay
articles.take_home: This study found that considering how age and frailty interact together provides better predictions of death risk after hip fracture surgery than treating them separately, with mortality predictions ranging from under 1% to over 30% depending on the combination of age, frailty level, and type of surgery. These personalised risk estimates could help doctors and patients make better decisions about which surgery is most suitable.

articles.title: Validation of the Bone-RADS (Bone Reporting and Data System) Score for Predicting Risk of Malignancy.
articles.authors: Bigness A, Zervoudakis G, Raso J, Stoy C, Kalos D, Joyce D, et al.
articles.population: Patients with lytic (hollow) bone lesions on extremity radiographs
articles.sample_size: 423 eligible radiographs (from 1,108 screened) with mean age 62 years
articles.outcomes: Bone-RADS score accuracy for predicting malignancy risk; sensitivity 97.1%, specificity 67.4%, inter-rater agreement (weighted kappa 0.52)
articles.take_home: The Bone-RADS scoring system is a useful tool for helping doctors decide which bone lesions might be cancerous, with very good ability to identify lesions that are likely to be harmless. However, doctors may interpret the scores differently from each other, so it works best as a practical guide rather than a definitive test.

articles.title: Early national comparison of robotic versus conventional hip replacements for arthritis using National Joint Registry data: target trial emulation study.
articles.authors: Mohammad HR, Judge A, Griffin XL, Murray DW
articles.study_type: Target trial emulation study using observational data
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip replacement for arthritis in UK hospitals
articles.sample_size: 666,283 hip replacements (656,080 conventional, 10,203 robotic) between 2018 and 2024
articles.outcomes: Five year implant survival, revision risk, malpositioning-related revision, intraoperative complications, patient survival
articles.take_home: Robotic and conventional hip replacements had similar survival rates and complication risks over five years. Robotic surgery showed a lower risk of revisions due to implant malpositioning, but costs substantially more and requires careful evaluation for NHS use.

articles.title: Prehospital whole blood transfusion in traumatic hemorrhagic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Ribeiro Junior MAF, Possiedi RD, Pacheco LS, de Cesaro Schpchacki N, Vieira LF
articles.population: Adult patients with traumatic hemorrhagic shock receiving prehospital treatment
articles.sample_size: 4040 patients across 6 studies (1558 receiving whole blood, 2482 receiving standard care)
articles.outcomes: 24-hour mortality, 28/30-day mortality, 6-hour mortality, in-hospital mortality, red blood cell transfusion requirements, and safety outcomes including acute respiratory distress syndrome, stroke and thrombotic events
articles.take_home: Prehospital whole blood transfusion did not improve survival rates compared to standard care in traumatic hemorrhagic shock. Whilst whole blood reduced the need for additional red blood cell transfusions within 24 hours of hospital arrival, this finding was not robust and the overall evidence quality was low to moderate.

articles.title: Fluoroscopy-assisted percutaneous management of posterior pelvic ring injuries via multiple transsacral and iliosacral screws in the supine position.
articles.authors: Zheng L, Shen X, Huang X, Chen J, Cao W, Yu L, et al.
articles.population: Patients with posterior pelvic ring injuries
articles.outcomes: Wound infection, neurovascular complications, screw position on CT, screw loosening, screw breakage, bone non-union
articles.take_home: Inserting multiple large screws through the skin to stabilise posterior pelvic ring fractures whilst the patient lies on their back was safe and effective, with no infections or nerve damage and excellent screw positioning in bone.

articles.title: CCBE1 promotes wound healing in diabetic rats by improving the functional impairment of AD-MSCs induced by AGEs.
articles.authors: Liang F, Mo J, Zhang J, Peng Z, Zhou J, Lu Y, et al.
articles.population: Human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells and Type 2 diabetic rats
articles.outcomes: Wound closure rate, cell proliferation and migration, blood vessel formation, skin regrowth, and VEGF protein levels
articles.take_home: In diabetic rats, stem cells modified to produce more CCBE1 protein closed wounds faster and promoted better blood vessel growth and skin healing compared to unmodified stem cells. This laboratory finding suggests a potential new approach to treating difficult-to-heal diabetic wounds, though human studies would be needed to confirm benefit.

articles.title: Locked plate fixation versus non-operative management for three and four-part proximal humeral fractures in elderly; A randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Abouelsoud M, Wahab MMA, Kamal HM, Mohamed AAA
articles.population: Elderly patients aged 65 years and older with three or four-part proximal humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes measured by DASH and Constant scores at 6 and 12 months; complications including shoulder-associated infections, stiffness, deformity and avascular necrosis
articles.take_home: At 12 months, elderly patients who received non-operative treatment with arm sling immobilisation had better functional outcomes than those who had surgery with a locked plate, with no significant difference in serious complications between the two approaches.
